title: Console Capacity Governor: unified fleet controls, scaling rules, and throughput audit trail
creator: Aisha Ng
description: Build a single Console pane (Capacity Governor) that lets operators manage fleet-level scaling controls, define autoscaling policy sets, set throughput guarantees per capacity pool, and inspect a chronological audit trail of policy changes and manual overrides. This ticket covers the PM scope: UI flows, acceptance criteria, rollout plan, and cross-team coordination tasks needed to ship with the runtime autoscaler and the change-logging backend.
goals: Expose scaling controls that map to Dedicated and Private fleet constructs (min/max instances, target RPS, reserved throughput)
Allow operators to author and attach autoscaling policy sets with deterministic evaluation order and previewed cost estimates
Surface a per-fleet throughput dashboard that correlates capacity, achieved p99 latency, and billing impact
Provide an immutable change history (who/when/why) with links to diffs and reversion actions
scope: Console UI: Capacity Governor primary view, policy editor modal, policy list, throughput insights chart, and change history timeline
Server: contract with ENG on API shape for policy CRUD, preview cost endpoint, and change-log events
Telemetry: wire up dashboard metrics (throughput, p50/p95/p99 latency, instance count, queued requests) and map to cost model
out_of_scope: On-prem installer changes for air-gapped deployments (separate ticket)
Deep policy language for per-customer custom scripting (future work)
Billing system changes beyond estimated cost preview
acceptance_criteria: Capacity Governor view is discoverable from Fleet page and respects RBAC (operators only)
Operators can create/edit/delete autoscaling policy sets and attach them to a fleet
Policy preview shows estimated cost delta and expected throughput uplift before save
Throughput dashboard shows last 72 hours with selectable time windows and overlays for policy changes
Change history records every policy save/attach/detach/override with user, timestamp, reason, and link to related PR or ticket
Can roll back to a previous policy state from the history view and the rollback creates a new auditable event
design_feedback: Design: emphasize small-multiple tiles for fleet summary then a full-width timeline for history (avoid crowding)
PM requested pre-populated policy templates (steady-state, bursty, conservative) with clear trade-offs
Accessibility: ensure keyboard flow and ARIA labels for timeline events and policy editor modal
UX asked for inline cost microcopy explaining assumptions used in cost preview
engineering_notes: ENG: APIs required - GET /fleets/{id}/policy, POST /fleets/{id}/policy, GET /fleets/{id}/metrics, GET /fleets/{id}/history
ENG: backend must emit change-log events to the audit store; front-end will consume a paginated history API
ENG: autoscaler accepts simplified policy DSL (min_instances, max_instances, target_rps, scale_window_seconds)
Perf: dashboard queries must be rate-limited and cached; suggested 1m roll-up for charts
rollout_plan: Phased rollout: 1) Feature behind feature flag for internal tenants, 2) Canary release to 3 pilot customers with Dedicated seats, 3) General availability with in-console guided tour and knowledge base article. Target GA after two pilot cycles and no SLO regressions for 7 days.
monitoring: Alerts: policy-apply-failure > 5% over 10m, rollback-triggered-alert when rollback occurs outside business hours
Quality metrics: percentage of policy-induced scale events matching expected range (to catch misconfigured policies)

change_history_summary: The change history must be an append-only timeline with event types: POLICY_CREATED, POLICY_UPDATED, POLICY_ATTACHED, POLICY_DETACHED, MANUAL_OVERRIDE, ROLLBACK. Each event must capture user id, user email, timestamp, change diff, and optional reason text. Events should be queryable by fleet, user, and time window and surface a direct action to rollback or create a follow-up change request. History items should include links to origin artifacts (ticket or PR) when available.
